parameters.name: APPLY_SD
parameters.help: Select 'Yes' to compute corrections to compensate for loss of amplitudes due to spherical wavefront spreading.

parameters.name: SDV_TYPE
parameters.help: Select between the 2 choices for spherical spreading corrections. (See P. Newman, Geophysics v. 38-03, p. 481.)

choices.label: 1/dist
choices.help: Corrections based on the reciprocal of the distance that the wavefront has travelled.

choices.label: 1/(time*vel**2)
choices.help: Corrections based on a function of travel time and velocity (assuming a layered earth).

parameters.name: APPLY_IE
parameters.help: Select 'Yes' to compute corrections to compensate for loss of amplitudes due to inelastic attenuation.

parameters.name: INLS_ATN
parameters.help: Constant inelastic attenuation value (alpha) used in: e**(alpha*x), where x = velocity * time.

parameters.name: db_bool
parameters.prompt: Get TAR velocity function from database?
parameters.help: A velocity function can either be retrieved from the database or specified by hand.

parameters.name: VELVARYS
parameters.help: Velocities may be spatially variant by CDP, but this will cause a longer run time.

parameters.name: DB_VEL
parameters.help: Use Mouse Button 1 to select an RMS velocity function parameter file from the parameter file menu.

parameters.name: TAR_VEL
parameters.help: Use MB1 to define the AVERAGE velocity function for true amplitude corrections (2-way time[in ms]-vel, time-vel, etc).

parameters.name: TAR_VEL2
parameters.help: Use MB1 to define the velocity functions for true amplitude corrections (2-way time[in ms]-vel, time-vel, etc).

parameters.name: APPLY_DB
parameters.help: Compute corrections by a simple deciBels per second amplitude adjustment function.

choices.label: Time zero
choices.help: dB/sec correction starts at time zero.

choices.label: Water bottom
choices.help: dB/sec correction starts at the water-bottom time.

parameters.name: DB_PER_S
parameters.help: This is the constant dB/sec value used to compute amplitude corrections.

parameters.name: APPLY_PW
parameters.prompt: Apply time raised to a power corrections?
parameters.help: Compute corrections by raising the time to a power and multiplying it by the sample value.

parameters.name: T_POWER
parameters.help: This is the constant to raise time to before multiplying by the trace samples.

parameters.name: TAR_MODE
parameters.help: Normally, gain is APPLIED, but for synthetic data you may wish to REMOVE amplitude effects.

choices.label: Apply
choices.help: This is the normal mode wherein seismic data are corrected for loss of signal strength.

choices.label: Remove
choices.help: This mode can be used to introduce Earth amplitude effects to synthetic data.

parameters.name: TIME_MAX
parameters.help: Maximum time in ms for computing TAR corrections. Beyond this time a constant scalar is applied. Use 0.0 for whole trace.

parameters.name: NORM_SRC
parameters.help: Computed gain curves are divided by normalization constant so that trace amplitudes are relatively unchanged.

parameters.name: REF_TIME
parameters.help: Reference time in ms for normalizing TAR corrections. Must not exceed length of trace. 0.0 defaults to middle of trace.
